hints.title: Cross-List Offset Neutralization Obstacle
hints.text: Comparing every pair of nodes takes quadratic time while extra collections consume linear space. How can traversing both paths in alternating succession neutralize any length difference?

hints.title: Switching Paths Length Neutralization Invariant
hints.text: Redirecting each pointer to the head of the opposite list upon reaching null equalizes the total traversed distance to lengthA + lengthB.

hints.title: Alternating Two-Pointer Traversal Procedure
hints.text: Initialize ptrA at headA and ptrB at headB. While ptrA is not equal to ptrB, advance ptrA to headB if ptrA is null else ptrA.next, and ptrB to headA if ptrB is null else ptrB.next. Return ptrA.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in list A (1 <= N <= 3 * 10^4)
M: number of nodes in list B (1 <= M <= 3 * 10^4)
complexity.notes: Both pointers traverse at most N + M steps before meeting at intersection or null.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Nested comparison takes O(N * M) time, timing out on lists of 30,000 nodes.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Alternating path redirection operates in strictly O(1) space without storing node addresses in auxiliary tables.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Knowing that two pointers traversing lengthA + lengthB meet at the exact intersection or simultaneously reach null if disjoint.
